brief.headline: Memory supercycle intact—DRAM +58–63% QoQ Q2, HBM4 allocation battle intensifies, hyperscaler capex hits $700bn
brief.summary: <cite index="17-1,17-18">Conventional DRAM contract prices projected to rise 58–63% QoQ in Q2 2026, following Q1's record 90–95% surge, while NAND climbs 70–75%.</cite> <cite index="24-5,24-9">Four largest hyperscalers will collectively spend roughly $700 billion on capex in 2026, nearly double 2025 levels.</cite> <cite index="2-5,2-27">UBS predicts SK Hynix will achieve ~70% market share in HBM4 for Nvidia's Rubin platform in 2026, while BofA forecasts HBM market to reach $54.6bn (+58% YoY).</cite> <cite index="32-1,32-6">TSMC nearly doubled CoWoS output to 75,000 wafers/month by end-2025 and projects 130,000/month by year-end 2026, with Nvidia securing 60% allocation.</cite> <cite index="9-3,9-4">Nvidia has begun signaling interest in 16-layer HBM for late-2026 delivery, forcing Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron into an accelerated development race.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: Long SK Hynix vs. Samsung. <cite index="2-1,2-2,2-4">SK Hynix secured world's first HBM4 mass production system last September and is expected to support two HBM generations (HBM3E and HBM4) by 2026.</cite> <cite index="44-1,44-12">Bernstein regression analysis suggests SK Hynix Q2 HBM revenue ~$7.5bn (+25% QoQ), vs. Samsung ~$4.7bn (+32% QoQ)—SK Hynix maintains larger absolute base and contract share.</cite> <cite index="44-8">HBM price resets expected early 2027 may favor SK Hynix more than Samsung given former's larger HBM contract share this year.</cite> <cite index="45-8">SK Hynix held 53% HBM market share in Q3 2025 vs. Samsung's 35%.</cite> <cite index="9-13,9-14">Samsung pivoting to hybrid bonding for 7th-gen 16-layer HBM4E due to prior adhesive-tech struggles, while SK Hynix maximizes industry-leading MR-MUF.</cite> SK Hynix has pricing power, execution momentum, and customer lock-in. Samsung is catching up but still second-tier in HBM qualification.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="2-13,2-14">BofA defines 2026 as 'supercycle similar to 1990s boom,' forecasting global DRAM revenue +51% YoY and NAND +45%, with ASPs rising 33% and 26% respectively.</cite> <cite index="5-9">AI will consume 20% of total DRAM production in 2026, with HBM's 3-to-1 wafer consumption ratio crowding out commodity DRAM capacity.</cite> <cite index="17-16">No credible near-term relief; new fab capacity not expected to reach meaningful volume before late 2027 or 2028.</cite> <cite index="13-5,13-6">Samsung and SK Hynix (70% global DRAM) signaled no aggressive capacity expansion, prioritizing profitability over volume—analysts project price rally extending past 2028.</cite> Structural supply-demand imbalance driven by hyperscaler LTAs, HBM capacity reallocation, and cleanroom lead times stretching years.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="2-18">BofA estimates 2026 HBM market at $54.6bn (+58% YoY).</cite> <cite index="2-19">Goldman Sachs forecasts HBM demand for custom ASIC-based AI chips will skyrocket +82%, accounting for one-third of market.</cite> <cite index="2-21,2-22">HBM3E remains flagship product in 2026; Nvidia Blackwell Ultra, Google, AWS selecting HBM3E for proprietary ASICs.</cite> <cite index="9-3,9-4,9-6">Nvidia signaling interest in 16-layer HBM for Q4 2026 delivery; performance evaluation expected before Q3.</cite> <cite index="9-11,9-12">16-layer HBM requires wafer thickness reduction to ~30μm (vs. 50μm for 12-layer); JEDEC caps HBM4 package at 775μm.</cite> <cite index="9-17,9-18">HBM3E to account for 66% of total HBM output in 2026 (down from 87% in 2025); competitive inflection point expected with Rubin launch in 2H26.</cite> <cite index="6-6,6-7">AMD MI400 features 12 HBM4 stacks (432GB on-package, ~19.6 TB/s bandwidth); early HBM4 modules deliver ~1.6 TB/s each.</cite> Intel/SoftBank ZAM alternative (2–3x HBM3 bandwidth) targeting 2029 commercialization poses long-term disruption risk.

news_pulse.headline: Korean retail dumping Nvidia, rotating into Samsung/SK Hynix via RIA accounts—78bn won Samsung, 66.7bn SK Hynix net bought
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="39-2,39-4,39-7">Investors realizing profits from US AI big tech/leveraged ETFs and rotating into Samsung (78bn won) and SK Hynix (66.7bn won); RIA balance at 1.94tr won, domestic assets 1.21tr won.</cite> Domestic momentum accelerating as 100% capital gains exemption expires end-May.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung/SK Hynix target price upgrades: Korea Investment 570k/3.8m won, Nomura 590k/4m won—stocks +8.51%/+11.17%
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="40-14,40-16,40-17">Successive target price hikes: Korea Investment 570k/3.8m won, Nomura 590k/4m won; stocks closed +8.51%/+11.17%.</cite> <cite index="40-10,40-11,40-12">Samsung operating profit forecast rose to 348tr won (from 301.6tr won a month ago); SK Hynix to 254tr won (from 207.9tr won).</cite> Sell-side revisions accelerating into earnings.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung averts general strike—tentative labor deal reached 90 min before walkout, bonuses/training exodus ongoing
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="42-2,42-9,42-10">Samsung reached tentative wage agreement with union a day before planned strike, just 90 min before walkout.</cite> <cite index="41-5,41-8,41-10">SK Hynix bonuses tipped to hit $477k this year, $900k next year; Samsung workers planning strike May 21 to extend continuous bonuses beyond semiconductor division.</cite> Production risk contained but labor cost pressures structural.

news_pulse.headline: Bernstein: Samsung Q2 HBM revenue $4.7bn (+32% QoQ), SK Hynix $7.5bn (+25% QoQ); HBM price resets favor SK 2027
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="44-3,44-4,44-5">Korea's multichip memory exports to Taiwan/Malaysia (HBM proxy) $3.7bn in April (-12% MoM on seasonality, +62% vs. Jan); Samsung HBM revenue regression $4.7bn Q2 (+32% QoQ).</cite> <cite index="44-11,44-12">SK Hynix April exports +4% MoM, +81% QoQ; Q2 HBM revenue ~$7.5bn (+25% QoQ).</cite> Export data confirms sequential momentum despite April softness.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity 130k wafers/month by late-2026 (vs. 75k end-2025); Nvidia locked 60%, Broadcom 15%, AMD 11%
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="30-1,30-3,30-4">Nvidia secured ~60% of TSMC's total CoWoS allocation for 2026, supporting Blackwell full-scale deployment and early Rubin ramp.</cite> <cite index="30-7,30-8">Broadcom ~15% for custom AI ASICs (Google/Meta); AMD ~11% for Instinct MI350/MI400.</cite> CoWoS bottleneck easing but Nvidia maintains structural moat.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: Q2 DRAM +58–63% QoQ, NAND +70–75%, following Q1's record +90–95% DRAM, +55–60% NAND
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="10-2,10-7,10-8">Q2 DRAM contract prices +58–63% QoQ, NAND +70–75% QoQ; follows Q1's record +90–95% DRAM, +55–60% NAND.</cite> <cite index="10-9,10-10">DRAM suppliers reallocating capacity to AI apps, NAND to enterprise SSDs; meaningful capacity expansion not expected until late 2027.</cite> Pricing deceleration off extreme base, but absolute levels remain elevated.

news_pulse.headline: Nvidia exploring 16-layer HBM for Q4 2026 delivery—wafer thickness must drop to 30μm, process changes required
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="9-3,9-4,9-5">Nvidia asked major memory suppliers if they could deliver 16-layer HBM in Q4 2026; discussions exploratory, no contracts, but triggered internal planning.</cite> <cite index="9-9,9-11">Transition from 12 to 16 layers 'technically much harder than 8 to 12'; wafer thickness must drop to ~30μm (vs. 50μm for 12-layer).</cite> Accelerated roadmap pressure favors SK Hynix execution track record.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler capex $700bn in 2026 (vs. $400bn 2025, $235bn 2024)—Meta raised guide to $125–145bn from $115–135bn
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="20-11,20-12">2024 combined capex of four biggest hyperscalers just over $200bn; 2026 on track to approach $700bn.</cite> <cite index="23-6">Meta raised full-year 2026 capex to $125–145bn from prior $115–135bn.</cite> <cite index="24-13,24-14,24-15,24-16">Q1 2026 QoQ capex: Meta $13bn→$20bn, Alphabet $17bn→$36bn, Microsoft $17bn→$31bn, Amazon $25bn→$44bn.</cite> Structural demand floor for HBM/memory intact.

brief.derivatives_signal: <cite index="42-3,42-7,42-8">Samsung premarket +6.16% to 293,000 won, SK Hynix +4.3% to 1.82m won on Nextrade (as of 8:05am May 21).</cite> <cite index="40-17">Prior session close: Samsung 299,500 won (+8.51%), SK Hynix 1.94m won (+11.17%).</cite> <cite index="43-4,43-9,43-10">Kiwoom Securities launched 20bn won ELS tied to Samsung/SK Hynix, targeting 32.1% annualized return, 3-year step-down with 85% early redemption barrier and 35% knock-in.</cite> Structured product issuance accelerating on rally—retail momentum and vol appetite both elevated. Option skew likely flattening; consider selling OTM puts to fund upside exposure.

Any Samsung/SK Hynix commentary on Q2 pricing discipline or HBM4 16-layer feasibility timeline—Nvidia's urgency creating negotiating leverage
TSMC remarks at Technology Symposium (May 14 event) on CoWoS/SoIC expansion cadence and customer allocation changes for 2H26
